name: Sandhill Crane Migration
unique: Half a million sandhill cranes pause on the Platte River at once, filling the air with a sound like a distant crowd and performing dancing courtship displays.
buzz: Sunrise blinds at Rowe are the way to see it; book months ahead. The noise and numbers are overwhelming in the best way.

name: Henry Doorly Zoo
unique: The world's largest indoor desert under a geodesic dome, a walk through rainforest and an aquarium with a shark tunnel, repeatedly ranked the best zoo in the country.
buzz: The desert dome is the showstopper; it takes a full day. Go on a weekday and take the skyfari.

name: Ashfall Fossil Beds
unique: A fossil bed where a volcanic ash fall killed a herd of rhinos, horses and camels 12 million years ago, now exposed in a working quarry.
buzz: The skeletons are still in the ground where they died, which is the fascinating part. Seasonal, so check dates.

name: Crane Trust
unique: A stretch of the Platte where half a million sandhill cranes stop each March, one of the largest bird migrations in the world.
buzz: The dawn blinds are the way to see them close and the season is short; book months ahead and bring warm clothes.

name: Joslyn Art Museum
unique: A free museum in a Art Deco building with European and American art, Native American works and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and strong, with a beautiful building and a good cafe. The Western art collection is the local specialty.

name: Museum of American Speed
unique: Three floors of race cars, engines and speed records, including land speed streamliners and a collection of pedal cars, in a building behind a parts warehouse.
buzz: Car people call it a hidden gem; the engine cutaway displays are beautiful. Allow three hours.

name: Niobrara River
unique: A spring fed river through the Sandhills with waterfalls, pine bluffs and a gentle current, one of the best floats in the Plains.
buzz: The water is clear and the trip is easy. Rent a tube or a canoe and go in summer.

name: Stuhr Museum of the Prairie Pioneer
unique: A 200 acre campus of relocated railroad town buildings around a lake, with a Pawnee earth lodge and a main building by Edward Durell Stone.
buzz: The living history town and the Pawnee lodge are the reasons to give it three hours; the main building is a architectural landmark of its own.

name: The Durham Museum
unique: A museum in the Art Deco Union Station, with trains, a soda fountain, a street of old storefronts and the history of the Union Pacific.
buzz: The station itself is gorgeous and the trains are the kid draw. Allow two hours.

name: Homestead National Historical Park
unique: The farm of the first homesteader under the 1862 act, with a tallgrass prairie restoration, a heritage center and the original claim cabin.
buzz: The prairie and the heritage center explain why the act changed the country; it is free and the trails are flat.

name: Lauritzen Gardens
unique: A 100 acre botanical garden with a conservatory, a model train garden, a rose garden and a woodland trail.
buzz: The model trains are the kid hit and the conservatory is the winter escape. Good in every season.

name: Nebraska State Capitol
unique: A 400 foot tower with a Nebraska life mural, a unicameral chamber and an observation deck with a view of the plains.
buzz: The building is one of the best state capitols, and the dome tour is worth it. Free.

name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
unique: A bluff that guided Oregon Trail wagons, with a summit road, trails and a museum of the westward migration.
buzz: The summit drive has the view and the trail is short. The Oregon Trail ruts are nearby.

name: Toadstool Geologic Park
unique: Badlands of mushroom shaped sandstone hoodoos and fossil beds, with a one mile loop through a landscape that looks like another planet.
buzz: It is remote, quiet and stunning at sunset; the dirt road is impassable when wet. Bring water.

name: Arbor Day Farm
unique: The farm where J. Sterling Morton started Arbor Day, with a tree adventure course, a orchard and a cider house on 260 acres.
buzz: The treehouse and the ropes course are the family draw and the history is the reason it exists; the fall apple harvest is the season.

name: Chimney Rock
customer: Oregon Trail people, road trippers, photographers
unique: The rock spire that guided every wagon train on the Oregon Trail, with a visitor center and a view of the Platte valley that has not changed much.
buzz: The landmark is smaller up close and that is the story; the center explains the trail and the walk to the base is short.

name: Golden Spike Tower
unique: An eight story tower over Union Pacific's Bailey Yard, the largest railroad classification yard in the world, where 10,000 cars are sorted every day.
buzz: Train people call it a pilgrimage and the view of the hump yard is mesmerizing; check the scanner feed and go when the light is good.

name: Old Market
unique: A warehouse district of cobblestone streets, brick buildings, galleries and restaurants, with horse drawn carriages and buskers.
buzz: The streets are photogenic and the food is good. Busy on weekend evenings.

name: Strategic Air Command and Aerospace Museum
unique: A hangar of Cold War bombers and missiles, including a B-36 and a SR-71, with a glass wall that lets you watch planes land at Offutt.
buzz: The B-36 is enormous and the Cold War exhibits are the history; aviation people say it is one of the best collections in the middle of the country.

name: Fontenelle Forest
unique: Nineteen hundred acres of oak and cottonwood forest along the Missouri with a boardwalk through the floodplain and bluffs that look over the river.
buzz: The boardwalk and the raptor program are the family stops and the birding is serious in spring; the bluffs trails are steep.

name: Museum of the Fur Trade
unique: A museum on the fur trade with a reconstruction of a trading post, a collection of trade guns and beads, and a garden of the plants the traders used.
buzz: The collection is serious and specific and the site is on the old fur route; it is small and the staff are experts.

name: Sheldon Museum of Art
unique: A free university art museum in a Philip Johnson building, with American art, modernism and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The building is the draw and the collection is free. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Buffalo Bill Ranch
unique: Buffalo Bill Cody's 1886 ranch house and barn, where the showman came home between tours, with longhorn cattle and a view of the Platte valley.
buzz: The barn and the house are the visit and the story of the Wild West show is the context; it is cheap and quiet.

name: Fort Kearny State Historical Park
customer: History families, trail people, school groups
unique: A frontier fort on the Platte that supplied every wagon train heading west, with rebuilt stockade and blacksmith shop and the trail ruts nearby.
buzz: The stockade and the demonstrations are the visit and the ruts are a short drive; it is quiet and cheap.

name: Hastings Museum
unique: A small city museum with a planetarium, a giant screen theater and the Kool-Aid exhibit, since the drink was invented here in 1927.
buzz: The Kool-Aid room is the quirky reason people stop and the planetarium is genuinely good; it is cheap and good with children.

name: Carhenge
unique: Thirty eight vintage cars buried nose down in a circle to replicate Stonehenge, built by a farmer as a family reunion joke and now a beloved landmark.
buzz: It is exactly as good as the premise; free and quick. The visitor center explains the replica's solstice alignments.

name: Chadron State Park
unique: Pine covered buttes and a canyon in the Pine Ridge, the oldest state park in Nebraska, with trails to a lookout and a swimming pool in summer.
buzz: The ponderosa forest feels like the Black Hills and the park is quiet; the trails are steep and the pool is a summer bonus.

name: Eugene T. Mahoney State Park
unique: A state park on the Platte with a lodge, a water park, horseback trails and a theater, built as a flagship park between Omaha and Lincoln.
buzz: The activity center and the pool are the family draw and the trails are easy; it is busy on summer weekends.

name: Great Platte River Road Archway
unique: A building that spans Interstate 80, with a museum on the overland trails that crossed here, from the Oregon Trail to the Lincoln Highway.
buzz: The architecture is the novelty and the exhibits are better than a roadside attraction needs to be; the view over the interstate is strange and fun.

name: Legacy of the Plains Museum
unique: A museum of dryland farming on the high plains with a collection of tractors, a windmill yard and a restored 1900s farmstead.
buzz: The machinery and the farmstead are good with children and the volunteers know the history; it pairs with Scotts Bluff.
